# Appendix B: Maintenance Schedule

## 2005 Honda CRV Recommended Maintenance Schedule

Proper maintenance extends vehicle life and ensures optimal performance. This appendix provides a comprehensive maintenance schedule based on manufacturer recommendations and industry standards.

---

## Oil and Filter Changes

| Service Interval | Frequency | Notes |
|------------------|-----------|-------|
| Oil and Filter Change | Every 7,500 miles or 6 months | Whichever comes first |
| First oil change | 1,000 miles or 1 month | Break-in period |
| Synthetic oil extension | Up to 10,000 miles | If using synthetic oil |

### Oil Change Checklist
- ☐ Drain old oil
- ☐ Replace oil filter
- ☐ Install new oil
- ☐ Check oil level after running
- ☐ Document mileage and date

---

## Air Filter Maintenance

| Service | Interval | Cost | DIY Possible |
|---------|----------|------|--------------|
| Engine Air Filter Replacement | Every 15,000-20,000 miles | $25-$40 | ✓ Yes |
| Cabin Air Filter Replacement | Every 12,000-15,000 miles | $35-$65 | ✓ Yes |

### Inspection Schedule
- Check air filters every 6,000 miles
- Replace if dirty or clogged
- Visual inspection during oil changes

---

## Fluid Levels - Check Every Month

| Fluid | Check Frequency | Service Interval | Cost |
|-------|-----------------|-----------------|------|
| Engine Oil | Monthly | Every 7,500 miles | $30-$60 |
| Coolant | Monthly | Every 30,000 miles | $40-$80 |
| Transmission Fluid | Quarterly | Every 30,000 miles | $100-$200 |
| Brake Fluid | Quarterly | Every 2 years | $50-$100 |
| Power Steering Fluid | Quarterly | Every 60,000 miles | $70-$120 |

### Fluid Check Procedures
1. Park on level surface
2. Engine cold (or 5 minutes after running)
3. Locate reservoir cap
4. Check level against minimum/maximum marks
5. Top up with approved fluid if low

---

## Tire Maintenance

| Service | Frequency | DIY | Cost |
|---------|-----------|-----|------|
| Tire Rotation | Every 7,500 miles | ✓ Yes | $0-$40 |
| Wheel Balance | Every 15,000 miles | ✗ No | $15-$30 |
| Tire Pressure Check | Weekly | ✓ Yes | $0 |
| Tire Replacement | Every 30,000-60,000 miles | ✗ No | $400-$800 |

### Recommended Tire Pressure
- Front: 32 PSI
- Rear: 32 PSI
- Check when tires are cold (before driving)

---

## Brake System

| Service | Interval | DIY | Cost |
|---------|----------|-----|------|
| Brake Pad Inspection | Every 15,000 miles | ✓ Possible | $0 |
| Brake Pad Replacement | Every 20,000-70,000 miles | ✗ No | $300-$600 |
| Brake Fluid Flush | Every 2 years | ✗ No | $100-$200 |

### Warning Signs
- ⚠️ Brake warning light on
- ⚠️ Soft or spongy brakes
- ⚠️ Grinding sounds when braking
- ⚠️ Longer stopping distances

---

## Spark Plugs and Ignition

| Service | Interval | Cost | Notes |
|---------|----------|------|-------|
| Spark Plug Replacement | Every 30,000 miles | $100-$200 | Consider gap adjustment |
| Ignition Coil Inspection | Every 30,000 miles | $0 | Visual check only |

---

## Seasonal Maintenance

### Spring Maintenance
- ☐ Check battery condition
- ☐ Inspect windshield wipers
- ☐ Check A/C system
- ☐ Rotate tires

### Summer Maintenance
- ☐ Check coolant level
- ☐ Verify air conditioning
- ☐ Inspect hoses for cracks
- ☐ Check tire pressure (increased with heat)

### Fall Maintenance
- ☐ Inspect battery (prepare for winter)
- ☐ Check heater functionality
- ☐ Replace wiper blades if worn
- ☐ Check fluid levels

### Winter Maintenance
- ☐ Use winter-grade oil if recommended
- ☐ Check battery charge
- ☐ Verify defroster operation
- ☐ Check traction/stability systems

---

## Annual Major Services (30,000, 60,000, 90,000 mile marks)

| Mileage | Recommended Services | Estimated Cost |
|---------|----------------------|-----------------|
| 30,000 | Air filter, fluid flush, inspection | $200-$400 |
| 60,000 | Transmission service, coolant flush | $300-$600 |
| 90,000 | Comprehensive inspection, brake service | $400-$800 |

## Emergency Service

### When to Seek Immediate Service

- Red oil pressure light
- Red engine temperature light
- Brake failure
- Loss of power steering
- Transmission slipping
- Smoke or flames from engine

### Recommended Emergency Kit

Keep in vehicle at all times:
- Jumper cables
- Spare tire
- Tire repair kit
- Basic tool kit
- Flashlight
- Flares or reflective triangles
- First aid kit
